title: QUIC RFC 9000 Preferred Address Connection ID Constraints
purpose: Describe the bounded transport-parameter and runtime enforcement for preferred_address connection-ID constraints, including zero-length mode rejection, sequence-1 accounting, and active_connection_id_limit counting.
design_summary: The transport-parameter codec validates preferred_address as a server-originated parameter with a non-zero, at-most-20-byte connection ID and rejects a server preference when the server selected zero-length connection IDs or reuses the handshake connection ID. Runtime peer transport-parameter commit repeats the preferred_address connection-ID constraint so direct TLS-state updates close with TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR. The peer connection-ID state records the preferred_address connection ID as sequence 1, counts it with the handshake connection ID against active_connection_id_limit, and leaves current path destination selection gated by the existing preferred-address migration path logic.
data_and_state_considerations: The preferred_address connection ID is tracked in the peer connection-ID history and active set as sequence 1 with its stateless reset token. It does not preempt the current destination connection ID on commit; the existing CurrentPeerDestinationConnectionId path transition gate selects it after the connection acts on the preferred address.
edge_cases_and_constraints: A server-selected zero-length initial_source_connection_id cannot be combined with preferred_address.
A zero-length preferred_address connection ID is rejected when parsing or formatting transport parameters.
The preferred_address connection ID cannot equal the server handshake connection ID.
The preferred_address connection ID length is encoded as one byte and capped at 20 bytes.
The handshake connection ID, preferred_address connection ID, and later NEW_CONNECTION_ID values are counted together when enforcing active_connection_id_limit.
Invalid preferred_address connection-ID constraints raised during peer transport-parameter commit close locally with TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR.
alternatives_considered: Rely only on broad transport-parameter round-trip tests; rejected because the selected requirements need focused proof and include runtime active-limit accounting.

Switch CurrentPeerDestinationConnectionId immediately to the preferred_address connection ID at transport-parameter commit; rejected because existing migration behavior intentionally waits until the preferred-address path transition is acted on.
Treat preferred_address connection-ID validation as only a parser concern; rejected because tests and TLS bridge seams can deliver structured transport parameters directly to runtime commit.
risks: The slice does not close the rest of S18P2 transport-parameter proof debt.
The preferred-address path transition remains owned by existing S9.6 migration behavior and is not broadened here.
This slice does not add benchmark coverage because it changes validation/accounting logic rather than a new parser hot path.

supplemental_sections.heading: Scope
supplemental_sections.content: This design covers preferred_address connection-ID constraints and accounting for S18P2. It does not claim complete preferred-address migration lifecycle closure or broad transport-parameter coverage cleanup.
